title: Subquery with IN
story: Which customers have placed at least one delivered order?
goal: Show the name of every customer who has a delivered order, alphabetically (column name).
starter:
SELECT name FROM customers
WHERE id IN ;

tests.label: Uses IN with a subquery or a JOIN
Hidden check on other data

hints: IN takes a list; a subquery can produce that list.
The inner query selects customer_id from orders where status is delivered.
SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered') ORDER BY name;
socratic: What list does the inner query give?
Why is a customer who ordered twice listed once?
How is this different from a JOIN?
explain: In one sentence: what does this query do, and why does it need the IN with a subquery or a JOIN?
solution: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered') ORDER BY name;
alt: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' ORDER BY c.name;
